nodes.label: Audio cue pinning test
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - pin-batch-c-12-files [ses_f17699447ffekdqy749bVRPTFE].md:L46] `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` is what catches a double cue. A test asserting only "something played" passes while a double stands. Also open each test with an `expectSilentSoFar()`-style precondition if the model file has one, so a cue on mount cannot be miscredited.

nodes.label: The audio cue coverage detector's matching depends on SOUND_EFFECTS call syntax, so raw audio literals defeat it
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - pin-batch-c-12-files [ses_f17699447ffekdqy749bVRPTFE].md:L11560] several of its siblings use raw strings (`"click_001.ogg"`, `"toggle_001.ogg"`) rather than `SOUND_EFFECTS`, which is exactly what the coverage detector's call-syntax matching depends on.
nodes.norm_label: the audio cue coverage detector's matching depends on sound_effects call syntax so raw audio literals defeat it

nodes.label: A plan status verdict needs verifiable evidence, not ticked checkboxes
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-26 - assess-2-snipset-plans-vs-acs [ses_f20934331ffeaXy4kqfeCRxcm2].md:L31] Neither is proof: a commit that touches a plan file records that the file changed, not that every acceptance criterion was met. A wrong "FINISHED" is much worse than an honest "INCONCLUSIVE", because the plan's status will be changed based on your answer.
nodes.norm_label: a plan status verdict needs verifiable evidence not ticked checkboxes
